title: Marcos urged anew: Declare El Niño state of calamity
summary: Senator Francis Pangilinan on Friday urged President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. anew to declare a state of calamity over the El Niño phenomenon to address budgeting shortfalls.

blocks.text: Senator Francis Pangilinan on Friday urged President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. anew to declare a state of calamity over the El Niño phenomenon to address budgeting shortfalls.

Pangilinan issued the statement during budget deliberations of the Department of Agriculture (DA) at the Senate. The DA and its attached agencies are asking for P203.56 billion for 2027, with Pangilinan serving as the budget sponsor in the upper chamber.
Senator Risa Hontiveros said 4.3 million farmers and fisherfolk are estimated to be affected by the El Niño phenomenon.
She asked Pangilinan how many of the affected farmers and fisherfolk would be able to receive aid or cash for work.
Citing data from the DA, Pangilinan said a P5-billion budget has been allotted for these sectors. From their ranks, 1.67 million farmers and fisherfolk could benefit from a P3,000-cash assistance.

The DA is also working with the Department of Social Welfare and Development and the Department of Labor and Employment for additional welfare programs. Rice farmers under the Rice Competitiveness Enhancement Fund will get P6 billion.
Pangilinan admitted that it is not enough.

"We are calling on the President to declare that state of national emergency calamity because as of November 2026, the calamity fund, disaster fund, is about P112 billion, so the response of Malacañang if I recall correctly is 'not yet,'" Pangilinan said.

"So, ibig sabihin (So, that means), they intend to, at the right time, but I'd like to think that the right time should be soon. Considering we don't want it to get worse before it gets worst. So that assistance is really necessary," he added.

Pangilinan added that Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. agreed that the declaration was needed to address the shortfall in the funding for 4.3 million farmers and fisherfolk affected by El Niño.
GMA News has reached out to Malacañang for comment, but it has yet to respond as of posting time.

Senators, through Senate Resolution 765, collectively called on the President earlier this month to declare a state of calamity under the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act in areas affected or threatened by the El Niño.

Under the law, a state of calamity would allow the President to impose price ceilings on basic necessities. Government or lending institutions may also grant non-interest loans to affected populations. — VDV, GMA News
